sentences.text: He further submitted that the petitioner is in custody since November, 2021 and in view of the fact that the prosecution has cited eighty four witnesses there is no likelihood of the trial being concluded in some reasonable time.
Accordingly he prays that the present petition be allowed and the petitioner be ordered to be released on bail.

3. The petition has been opposed by the State, inter alia, on the ground that the offences alleged to have been committed by the petitioner alongwith other coaccused are grave and heinous and further the petitioner happens to be the resident of State of Utter Pradesh and seven other FIRs registered against the petitioner in the State of Utter Pradesh and Delhi, if released on bail there is each and every possibility that he might jump the bail and thus may evade the trial.

Learned Additional Advocate General further submitted that otherwise also as the statements of some of the material witnesses have not yet been recorded, therefore also if released on bail, there is a possibility that he may try to win over the witnesses and create impediment in the course of fair trial.

Learned Additional Advocate General also submitted that as the investigation which has been carried out by the police clearly proves the involvement of the petitioner in the crime, therefore also the petitioner does not deserves to be released on bail.

. 
4. I have learned counsel for the parties and have also taken into consideration the status report filed by the State as also the documents appended with the petition.

5. A perusal of the order passed by the Court of learned Additional Sessions JudgeI, Una, District Una, H.P., dated 04.10.2023 demonstrates that the bail petition of the petitioner was rejected by the learned Trial Court by assigning cogent reasons and learned counsel for the petitioner has not been able to demonstrate before this court that there is any change in circumstance so as to warrant any interference in favour of the petitioner at this stage.

sentences.text: 6. It is settled law that while considering a bail application, primarily the Court has to take into consideration the gravity of the offences alleged to have been committed by the accused; the possibility of the petitioner jumping the bail if released and thus not being available for the purpose of trial and; possibility of the petitioner again indulging in same offence, if released on bail for which he stands apprehended.

Besides this, the offences alleged to have been committed by the petitioner are indeed grave and heinous and taking into consideration the fact that there are seven cases registered against the petitioner in the State of Utter Pradesh and Delhi including the offences under the provisions of Indian Penal Code and Arms Act etc., this Court has reasons to believe that there is a possibility that in case the petitioner is ordered to be released on bail, he may again commit the same offence.
